newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end short session mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end short session mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished a holiday-shortened session mostly lower and in the lower part of the day's ranges.
Volume was light as many traders extended their Thanksgiving holiday for another day, making for thin trading conditions.
"This is what you would expect after the holiday. There's not much activity," said one currency trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Currency futures closed at 1200 CST/1800 GMT after the Thanksgiving Day holiday on Thursday. Trading hours return to normal on Monday.
The dollar firmed Thursday after Bank of France monetary council member Jean-Pierre Gerard called for a stronger dollar.

However, activity was so light the dollar failed to build up enough momentum to penetrate resistance at 1.5400 marks and 114.00 yen, equal to support in the December mark at about $0.6499 and in the December yen at about $0.008755.

At settlement, December yen futures fell $0.000042 to $0.008802, marks were off $0.0042 to $0.6508, Swiss francs fell 0.0068 to $0.7683, sterling was up $0.0072 to $1.6812, the Canadian dollar was off $0.0020 at $0.7417, the Australian dollar was up $0.0033 to $0.8142 and the peso eased $0.000150 to $0.125300. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
